text.p: Germany's Siemens AG and computer networking group 3Com Corp said on Wednesday they had formed an alliance to jointly market and develop voice and data networking products.
The pact calls for SIemens' private communications unit (PN) to market 3Com's computer networking products worldwide and to license network control software from the California company.

They also planned to develop new products that integrate SIemens' Hicom telephones with 3Com networking cards, switches and routers, and aimed to generate $500 million from the collaboration over the next five years.

The alliance should allow the companies "to serve a substantially expanded user base by offering advanced networking infrastructures for integrated and multimedia data," said Ron Sege, head of 3Com's global products group.
PN president Dietrich Botsch said the worldwide market for business communications systems was growing 15 percent annually, and would be worth 190 billion marks by the year 2000.

The companies declined to say how much they would invest in their development effort. The work would be directed by a team in Boston and carried out largely in Israel and Santa Clara, Calif., where both already have engineering centers.
The agreement is not exclusive as Siemens already markets products from competitors of 3Com. Botsch said the companies had no plans to form a joint venture.

Sege said the pact complemented the companies' June agreement to cooperate in wide-area networking products. "The agreement we are talking about today is focused on local-area networks within companies," he said.

The jointly developed products would enable companies to make internal phone calls over their computer networks instead of maintaining a separate lines for voice calls. "Today voice and data are divided worlds," Botsch said.
The products should also make it possible to have a single phone number that could receive phone calls, voice mail, electronic mail and faxes, Sege said.
On the Internet, their voice/data products would enable a user to view a retailer's sales catalog and click on a picture of a product to place a voice call to a sales representative.
